facts.claim: A marriage licence for a foreign national legally residing in Greece is issued by the competent department of the municipality of residence; the competent body for the procedure is the Ministry of Interior.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Residents of Greece only. Not the route for couples living in the UK.

facts.claim: 'The mayor or the president of the community shall wait for one week from the date of submission of the relevant application for any possible objection by third parties.' Deadline of completion: 7 days; the licence is granted immediately after expiry of the one-week period if there is no objection.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Resident route. See F-15 (8 days end to end on the civil-licence entry).

facts.claim: The clock starts on the date the application is submitted; staff check all documents and the newspaper notice, then issue a protocol number. Incomplete applications are returned and the procedure starts again.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Fee for issuing the licence to a foreign resident: EUR 18, paid as an e-paravolo (code 2386).
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Resident licence only. The civil-licence entry for residents (F-15) says 'provided without cost'.

facts.claim: The licence is valid for 6 months.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Documents for the foreign-resident licence include a certificate of no impediment from the competent consular or other authority, a birth certificate translated into Greek, proof of residence, passport or residence permit, a translated divorce decree if relevant, and the newspaper issue carrying the marriage announcement.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Residents only.

facts.claim: Documents from Hague Convention countries are accepted only with an Apostille and 'translated into Greek by a Greek translator'.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: UK apostilles come from the FCDO Legalisation Office (see UK facts).

facts.claim: Legal basis: Civil Code articles 1368 to 1370; Law 1250/1982 (civil marriage); PD 391/1982; Law 5089/2024 (marriage between persons of the same sex).
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Athens Civil Marriages Department serves permanent residents of the City of Athens and Greek citizens abroad registered in Athens; applicants appear in person with ID. 'The marriage license is issued seven (7) days after the submission and verification of the required documents and is valid for six (6) months.'
facts.use_note: Athens publishes no route for foreigners living abroad.

facts.claim: Athens: every document lodged must have been issued within the last six months; a home-country marital status certificate must have been issued within the last three months. Foreign residents need a home-country marriage licence with Apostille, or a Certificate of No Impediment from the home country or its Embassy in Greece, officially authenticated and translated into Greek, plus an authenticated, translated birth certificate.

Whether you can get married abroad depends on local laws. You need to check the laws in the country where you want to marry, find out the process, and check which documents you need to prove you are free to marry. You can get advice from the person conducting the ceremony, the authority that registers marriages in that country, or a wedding planner.
facts.use_note: gov.uk/marriage-abroad/y/greece now redirects to this generic guide; there is no longer a Greece-specific gov.uk marriage page.

facts.claim: Some countries may ask for documents to prove you are free to marry, for example a certificate of no impediment or a marital status affirmation. The gov.uk online service lets you check which documents you might need and apply and pay for them. You must have a valid British passport to use this service. Once started, an application cannot be saved and times out after 30 minutes of inactivity.
facts.use_note: Online service: prove-eligibility-foreign-government.service.gov.uk. The guide does not name the document Greece requires or its fee; see gaps.

facts.claim: When you marry abroad, the authorities in that country register it in their national civil records. 'You cannot get a UK marriage or civil partnership certificate if your marriage or civil partnership happened abroad. Only UK marriages and civil partnerships are registered in the UK.'
facts.use_note: Key correction for UK readers: there is no UK registration of a Greek marriage. Keep the Greek certificate.

facts.claim: A foreign marriage is recognised in the UK if it was lawful in the country where it took place and it would be allowed under UK law. You may want to get your foreign certificate translated, which can help if you plan to use it outside the country where it was issued. If you want a UK marriage certificate, you can choose a legal ceremony in the UK and a commitment ceremony abroad.

FCDO entry requirements for Greece (full 'British citizen' passport): Greece follows Schengen rules. The passport must have a date of issue less than 10 years before the date you arrive, and an expiry date at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen area. You can travel without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period as a tourist or to visit family or friends.
facts.use_note: The travel advice has no wedding-specific notes. It says to contact the Greek Embassy in the UK if unsure how entry rules apply. Watch the 10-year issue date rule for older passports.

facts.claim: The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) is being implemented across Schengen; Greek authorities have indicated that they will not collect biometric data (fingerprints and photos) for UK travellers as part of EES.
facts.use_note: Optional travel note. Can change; recheck before publishing.

facts.claim: The FCDO Legalisation Office legalises UK public documents (for example a birth, marriage or death certificate from a public registry, or documents certified by a UK notary or solicitor) by attaching an apostille. It cannot legalise documents issued outside the UK. Birth, marriage and other General Register Office certificates cannot get an e-Apostille; they need a paper-based apostille.
facts.source_date: page shows dateModified 2015-02-25; fees live on 2026-11-20
facts.use_note: So a UK birth certificate for Greece needs a paper apostille.

facts.claim: Legalisation fees per document: Standard (paper-based) GBP 45 plus courier or postage; e-Apostille GBP 35. Courier return within the UK GBP 6 per 1.5kg. Standard service usually takes up to 25 working days plus courier or postage time; e-Apostille up to 2 working days.
facts.use_note: Write as GBP 45 per document (paper). Up to 25 working days is the main timing risk for UK couples.

facts.claim: FCDO consular fee 11: 'Issuing a certificate that no impediment to an intended marriage or civil partnership has been shown to exist, or issuing any local equivalent document for an intended marriage ... in accordance with local law': GBP 50 (in English or any other language). Fee 10, receiving notice of an intended marriage: GBP 50. Fees are charged in British pounds and are the same in every country.
facts.use_note: Medium: this is the general consular fee schedule. Which document Greece needs from a UK resident (CNI, or another document) and the total charged by the online service are shown only inside the application flow, which could not be read. Say 'the FCDO consular fee for a CNI or local equivalent is GBP 50 per document' and confirm the Greece outcome in the gov.uk service.

facts.claim: HM Passport Office: you can get a new passport in your new name before or after the ceremony. After the ceremony, send your marriage certificate when you apply in your new name (including double-barrelled names). Online application costs GBP 102; paper costs GBP 115.50. You do not need a new passport if you marry but keep your name. The name on your passport must match the one you use when you book travel.
facts.use_note: Book flights to Greece in your current passport name.

facts.claim: You can apply for a passport in your new name up to 3 months before the ceremony; the new passport is post-dated and cannot be used before the ceremony, and your old one is cancelled. You must send a 'passports for newly weds and civil partners' form signed by the religious minister or registrar who will conduct the ceremony. Some countries will not issue visas for post-dated passports.
facts.use_note: Do not recommend this for a Greek wedding: you would travel on a passport not valid until the ceremony, and the form must be signed by the Greek officiant. Whether that works abroad is not stated. Advise changing name after the wedding.

facts.claim: A foreign marriage certificate is a non-UK document: the FCDO Legalisation Office cannot legalise documents issued outside the UK; they must be legalised in the country where they were issued.
facts.use_note: If a UK body wants a Greek certificate apostilled, that apostille comes from Greece. Which Greek authority issues it is a gap.

facts.claim: Ministry of Interior circular 1969/S.477 of 4 January 2019: a foreign public document certifying that a foreign national has no impediment to marrying in Greece is equivalent to a marriage licence under Greek law when it also names the other future spouse, so a Greek marriage licence need not be issued.
facts.publisher: Hellenic Ministry of Interior, Directorate of Civil and Municipal Status
facts.use_note: KEY for non-resident UK couples. Medium because the PDF was decoded by hand from a legacy Greek font. Whether the UK document from the gov.uk service names the intended spouse is a gap. Confirmation sits with the town hall, never the Wedded Advisor.

facts.claim: Same circular: an essential precondition for foreigners to marry in Greece is an official document (passport, visa, residence permit and so on) showing they are lawfully present in Greece.

Chania, foreigners living abroad: bring an original marriage licence from your own country's competent authority, translated and certified, showing its validity period and naming the person you will marry; if it does not name the other person, it is not accepted. Also a recent birth certificate, a recent family status certificate where your country issues one, a recent passport copy, the municipality's application form and a Law 1599/86 solemn statement. Hague-country documents need an Apostille; originals, not photocopies. Documents may be lodged in person or by email (politikoi-gamoi@chania.gr).
facts.publisher: Municipality of Chania, Civil Marriages Office
facts.use_note: No newspaper notice, Greek licence or one-week wait on Chania's non-resident list. One municipality's rules only.

facts.claim: Heraklion, foreigners NOT residing permanently in Greece: a marriage licence from their own country translated into Greek with an Apostille; a birth certificate translated into Greek with an Apostille; and 'a residence permit or VISA (whose validity period has not expired)'. Each person marrying must be accompanied by an adult witness (a relative is allowed) with ID or passport.
facts.use_note: Two witnesses in total at Heraklion. Other municipalities may differ.

facts.claim: Heraklion civil ceremony fees under City Council decision 906/2007: EUR 100 for Tuesday or Thursday at 12:00; EUR 150 for Wednesday or Friday from 18:00, in the Municipal Council Hall.
facts.use_note: One municipality's published fees; confirm with the town hall.

facts.claim: From 1 September 2021 a simplified official-translation procedure replaced the old MFA translation procedure: you choose a translator from the Electronic Register of Certified Translators (metafraseis.services.gov.gr) and contact them directly (Law 4781/2021). Register translators officially translate foreign public documents into Greek, provided Hague-country documents carry an Apostille.
facts.use_note: The 'MFA translation department' in the old article is outdated.

facts.claim: 'In order for the marriage to take place, whether as a civil marriage or as a marriage solemnised by the Eastern Orthodox church, a licence is required by the mayor of the last place of residence, of each of the persons to be married.' The residents' civil-licence entry lists 'Deadline of completion: 8 days' (one-week objection wait plus one day to grant), 'Provided without cost', validity 6 months; if the marriage does not take place within six months of the newspaper notice, the notice must be repeated.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: A marriage certificate (lixiarchiki praxi gamou) presupposes the religious or civil marriage has been registered at the registry office of the municipality where it took place (Law 344/1976). Copies are free, 10-day completion deadline, from municipalities, KEP centres, or digitally on gov.gr with TAXISnet credentials.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: Law 5089/2024 (Gazette A 27/2024) provides for civil marriage between persons of the same sex and is cited as a legal basis on the gov.gr licence entries.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Civil only. Corrects the old article.

facts.claim: Greek Embassy London, 'Issuance of Marriage License': the bride and groom attend the Consular Office with passport or ID and each completes an application, an authorisation and a Solemn Declaration of No Impediment to Marriage; the documents go to an authorised person who submits them to the competent Municipality for the marriage licence and birth certificate. Fees: declaration EUR 10, copy EUR 10, or equivalent in sterling.
facts.publisher: Embassy of Greece in London (Hellenic Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
facts.use_note: This route is for people registered with a Greek municipality, in practice Greek citizens. Useful only for a UK couple where one partner is Greek. The Embassy's consular civil ceremony in London is for Greek citizens only (per search snippet of mfa.gr/uk, not read in full).

legal.summary: Proof of freedom to marry (CNI or equivalent) is applied for online via gov.uk; valid British passport required.
A marriage abroad is not registered in the UK and no UK certificate is issued; it is recognised if lawful locally and allowed under UK law (F-14).
UK birth certificates need a paper apostille from the FCDO Legalisation Office.
A foreign no-impediment document naming the spouse replaces the Greek licence for foreigners (2019 circular).
Chania non-resident document list; confirm with the town hall.
Heraklion non-resident document list and two witnesses; confirm with the town hall.
Official translations via MFA Register of Certified Translators since 2021.

prices.item: Greek marriage licence for foreign residents (e-paravolo)
FCDO apostille, standard paper, per document
prices.amount: GBP 45 plus courier or postage (e-Apostille GBP 35, not available for GRO certificates)

prices.item: FCDO consular fee: CNI or local equivalent document
New UK passport in married name
Greek Embassy London solemn declaration (Greek-registered partner only)

old_article_claims.title: If You're Thinking of Getting Married in Greece You Need to Know This
old_article_claims.overall_verdict: Outdated and written for Australian couples. Roughly 4 of 18 claims supported; several legal claims are wrong (same-sex marriage, MFA translation service, newspaper notice timing, celebrant) and no UK steps appear.

claims.claim: More and more Australian couples are choosing Greece.
claims.note: Wrong audience for the UK refresh; no source.

claims.claim: You don't need to be a Greek resident to marry in Greece.
If marrying a Greek citizen or resident, they must hold a valid residence permit.
claims.note: Not stated by any official source read; Greek citizens do not need a residence permit.

claims.claim: Civil unions are performed by a celebrant; religious ones require a priest.
claims.note: Greek civil marriage is licensed and conducted through the mayor or municipality (F-29, F-26), not a celebrant. 'Civil union' is the wrong term.

claims.claim: Same-sex civil unions are permitted but marriages are not legally recognised.
Waiting from a few days to a few months; civil authorities take up to a week.
claims.note: One-week wait applies to the Greek licence for residents; non-resident lists (Chania, Heraklion) show no wait. 'Few months' unsourced.

claims.claim: Documents must not be dated more than three months before the wedding date.
claims.note: Athens: six months for documents, three months for marital status certificate, measured at lodging, not the wedding date. Varies by town hall.

claims.claim: Couples can apply themselves or hire a Greek-based wedding planner.
claims.note: gov.uk lists a wedding planner as one source of advice (F-11); legal confirmation still sits with the municipality.

claims.claim: Licence valid for six months.
Within that time the couple submits a joint application to the mayor confirming date and location.
Newspaper notice at least eight days before applying for a licence is required for the marriage to be legal.
claims.note: Newspaper notice applies to the residents' licence route (F-06, F-29); no official source gives 'eight days before applying'. Absent from non-resident lists (F-25, F-26).

claims.claim: Foreign documents need a Hague Apostille.
Non-Hague countries verify documents at the Foreign Ministry or Greek Embassy.
claims.note: Not relevant to UK (a Hague state); not checked.

claims.claim: Translations can be certified by a lawyer, the foreign ministry's translation department, a certified translator or the Greek consulate.
claims.note: MFA translation service replaced in 2021 by the Register of Certified Translators. Some town halls still list lawyers and consulates.

claims.claim: Proof of freedom to marry or a notarised affidavit in English and Greek.
claims.note: UK route is the gov.uk online service (CNI or equivalent). Some towns want a document naming the spouse.

claims.claim: Two witnesses with passports or Greek ID for civil ceremonies.
Civil fees: EUR 7 affidavit, EUR 200 to 500 documentation, about EUR 100 translation.
claims.note: No official source. Replace with F-18, F-19, F-27.

claims.claim: Religious wedding only if both are baptised Christians; non-Orthodox party needs baptism certificate and statement children will be baptised Orthodox.
claims.note: No official Church of Greece source read.

claims.claim: Catholic wedding needs bishop's written permission and Pre-Cana certificate.
Couples must obtain a marriage certificate within 40 days or be fined; unregistered marriages aren't valid.
claims.note: Registration at the municipality is confirmed (F-30); the 40-day deadline, the fine and the 'not valid' consequence are not confirmed by any official page read.

needs.what: Which document Greece requires from a UK resident via the gov.uk online service (CNI, marital status affirmation, or other), its total fee, validity period and whether it names the intended spouse. The service only shows this inside the application flow.
needs.who: planning team (run the gov.uk checker for Greece and screenshot) or a couple's real application

needs.what: Current practice for UK non-residents at Thira (Santorini) and Mykonos town halls: documents, newspaper notice, wait, translations. No official page found.
needs.who: Wedded Advisor to gather; legal confirmation from the town hall itself

needs.what: A real UK couple's Greek wedding timeline with consent (optional).

gaps.detail: gov.uk/marriage-abroad/y/greece now redirects to the generic guide. There is no published British Embassy Athens wedding page on gov.uk; the Greece-specific outcome lives inside the prove-eligibility-foreign-government.service.gov.uk application flow, which could not be read.
No official page read gives the validity period of the UK document. Athens says documents must be issued within six months of lodging (F-10). Do not state a UK validity period.

nrscotland.gov.uk 'getting married abroad' returns 404; GRO Northern Ireland (nidirect) not read. gov.uk F-13 states UK-wide that only UK marriages are registered in the UK. A law-firm snippet says Scotland no longer registers overseas marriages (not a citable source). Use F-13 only.

gaps.topic: Apostille on the Greek marriage certificate
gaps.detail: Issuing Greek authority for apostilles on municipal certificates not confirmed. HMPO accepts the marriage certificate for name change (F-20) but whether it needs a translation or apostille for HMPO is not stated.
Not confirmed on an official page (carried over from the 12 Nov research).

gaps.topic: Greek Embassy London role for British couples
gaps.detail: No mfa.gr/uk page offers a service for two British nationals marrying in Greece. Its marriage-licence page serves Greek-registered persons (F-32). Commercial claims that the Embassy must 'verify translations' are not from an official source and must not be used.
All legal steps are confirmed with the Greek municipality (town hall) where the wedding takes place, and on the UK side with the FCDO via gov.uk; never the Wedded Advisor.
